v1_to_v2_changes: Evidence-class-driven source routing (cheapest capable, not sequence)
EVIDENCE_QUESTION object (question → hypothesis → impact → source → stop condition)
Robust stopping logic (coverage + quality + diversity + adversarial success, not count)
SEARCH_INCOMPLETE independent from engineering failure (V8 pattern)
FDA/clinical reserved for final portfolio audit (not in discovery loop)
Pushing-the-envelope rule encoded: guilty until survives attack

doctrine.pushing_the_envelope_rule: The machine should behave as though every invention is guilty until it survives attack. Find the strongest plausible competing mechanism. Determine whether it actually solves the same constrained problem. If it does, compare mechanisms. If it wins, the invention changes or dies. If it loses, generate the next strongest alternative. Then attack the surviving architecture with a new evidence source and a harder operating condition. The pipeline should therefore seek CONTRADICTION and INFORMATION GAIN, not confirmation.
doctrine.implementation_principle: One canonical orchestrator. Do not create separate competing research engines for each territory.

research_loop.v1_limitation: V1 was stage-driven (8 rigid stages). V2 is question-driven.
v2_loop: result → UNCERTAINTY (what do we still not know?)
attack again with new evidence source or harder condition
repeat until: SURVIVOR (mechanism survives all attacks) or CEILING (genuine negative) or EXHAUSTED (no more questions)

loop_termination.SURVIVOR: mechanism survives all generated attacks AND no more uncertainty questions remain
loop_termination.CEILING: strongest alternative matches or beats candidate on same coupled problem
loop_termination.EXHAUSTED: no more credible attack questions can be generated (coverage complete)

research_loop.loop_continuation: always — if uncertainty remains, generate next question

schema.question: string — the specific uncertainty to resolve
schema.hypothesis: string — what we expect to find

expected_decision_impact.if_found: how the result changes the invention state
expected_decision_impact.if_not_found: how the absence changes the state

schema.evidence_class: discovery | mechanism | architecture | hostile_prior_art | engineering | patent | clinical
schema.cheapest_capable_source: source selected by routing rules (not rigid sequence)
schema.stop_condition: when to stop searching (e.g., 'top 10 results all classified', '0 relevant hits after focused query')
schema.result: FOUND | NOT_FOUND | AMBIGUOUS | FALSE_POSITIVE (filled after execution)

example_questions.question: Does any prior art teach active valve perturbation for hydraulic parameter estimation in a CSF-venous shunt?
example_questions.hypothesis: No — active interrogation is architecturally distinct from passive observation

expected_decision_impact.if_found: Position #1 novelty destroyed — escalate to claim chart
expected_decision_impact.if_not_found: Position #1 survives this attack — generate next question
expected_decision_impact.if_ambiguous: Run PatSnap semantic-search using closest patent as seed

example_questions.cheapest_capable_source: PatentBear (free Boolean) → PatSnap (claim-data if threat found)
example_questions.stop_condition: top 10 PatentBear results classified + top 5 PatSnap semantic hits claim-audited

example_questions.question: Does passive ML (without active perturbation) perform as well as active interrogation?
example_questions.hypothesis: No — active perturbation adds discriminative value

expected_decision_impact.if_found: Position #1 mechanism destroyed by passive ML — CEILING
expected_decision_impact.if_not_found: Position #1 mechanism validated — generate harder disturbance question
expected_decision_impact.if_ambiguous: Test with stronger ML (deep learning) or harder noise

example_questions.stop_condition: ≥3 ML algorithms tested (SVM/RF/KNN) on MEDIUM noise with ≥200 samples/state

source_routing_v2.principle: The orchestrator chooses the CHEAPEST source CAPABLE of answering the question. Not a rigid sequence.

discovery.rationale: Free, broad coverage. Use for concept mapping and author/affiliation tracking.

mechanism.rationale: Peer-reviewed literature reveals mechanisms and alternative architectures. Scopus TITLE-ABS-KEY gives focused results.

architecture.rationale: Cross-source: Scopus/Lens for scientific architectures, PatentBear for patented ones.

hostile_prior_art.rationale: PatentBear free for Boolean + claim extraction. PatSnap only for top ≤10 highest-threat patents (cost gate).

engineering.rationale: Engineering questions answered by simulation, not external search.

patent.rationale: PatSnap only for residual high-value patent uncertainty. Must pass cost gate.

clinical.rationale: RESERVED for final portfolio audit. NOT in 1-10 discovery loop.

source_routing_v2.cost_gate_rule: Every source selection must answer: 'Is this the cheapest source capable of answering this question?' If a cheaper source can answer, use it. If not, escalate.
source_routing_v2.information_gain_gate: Every call must answer: 'What uncertainty will this call eliminate?' If 'none', don't execute.

equivalence_engine_v2.core_principle: 'Same problem' requires comparison on 6 axes, not just keyword overlap.

axis_1_objective.description: What clinical/technical problem does each solve?
axis_1_objective.example_match: Both solve CSF drug exposure enhancement
axis_1_objective.example_mismatch: Position #2 (CSF drainage + retention) vs hydrogel (SCI drug delivery) — different objectives

axis_2_mechanism.description: What physical principle does each use?
axis_2_mechanism.example_mismatch: Position #2 (size-selective filter) vs hydrogel (sustained-release depot) — different mechanisms

axis_3_constraints.example_mismatch: Position #2 (drainage maintained) vs hydrogel (no drainage constraint) — different constraints

axis_4_operating_environment.example_match: Both operate in endovascular CSF shunt
axis_4_operating_environment.example_mismatch: Position #2 (eShunt lumen) vs hydrogel (intrathecal injection) — different environments

axis_5_output.example_match: Both deliver therapeutic agent to CSF
axis_5_output.example_mismatch: Position #2 (filtered CSF + retained drug) vs hydrogel (sustained drug release) — different outputs

axis_6_failure_mode.example_mismatch: Position #2 (filter fouling) vs hydrogel (depot depletion) — different failure modes

classification.SAME_PROBLEM_SAME_MECHANISM: All 6 axes match → threatens novelty. Escalate to claim chart.
classification.SAME_PROBLEM_DIFFERENT_MECHANISM: Objective + constraints match, but mechanism/output differ → architecturally distinct. Run engineering comparator.
classification.NEIGHBORING_PROBLEM: Objective overlaps but constraints/environment/output differ → does not threaten. Record in FALSE_POSITIVE ledger.

equivalence_engine_v2.v1_to_v2_improvement: V1 used 5 questions. V2 uses 6 axes including FAILURE_MODE — this prevents hydrogel-like neighboring solutions from being treated as genuine threats.

stopping_logic_v2.v1_limitation: V1 used 'CEILING after ≥3 alternatives' — mechanical shortcut. Three weak alternatives should never terminate a territory.
stopping_logic_v2.v2_rule: Stopping depends on COVERAGE + EVIDENCE_QUALITY + MECHANISM_DIVERSITY + ADVERSARIAL_SUCCESS, not count.

required: ALL generated attack questions have been executed
Coverage = COMPLETE (Lens + Scopus + PatentBear + PatSnap all searched, no SEARCH_INCOMPLETE)
Mechanism diversity = HIGH (≥3 materially different alternative mechanisms tested)
Adversarial success = candidate beats ALL same-problem alternatives on pre-registered metrics
Strongest alternative matches or beats candidate on SAME coupled problem
AND alternative survives equivalence test (6-axis match on objective + constraints)
AND engineering comparator shows alternative ≥ candidate on primary metric
CEILING_negative_freeze.result: BELOW_BUYER_THRESHOLD — freeze negative ceiling, move to next territory

required: No more credible attack questions can be generated
Mechanism diversity = HIGH (≥3 materially different alternatives tested)
EXHAUSTED.result: WOULD_CONSIDER_WITH_MILESTONES — survive with milestones, move to next territory

do_not_terminate_if: Alternatives are not materially different (e.g., same mechanism with minor variation)
Adversarial success not demonstrated (no engineering comparator run)
stopping_logic_v2.mechanism_diversity_check: Alternatives must use DIFFERENT physical principles, not just different parameters. E.g., 'threshold vs ML' is mechanism diversity; 'SVM vs RF' is NOT (both are ML).

false_positive_state.definition: A search result that is REAL but IRRELEVANT to the invention. The system records why it was rejected rather than silently discarding.
false_positive_state.example: Position #1 Scopus 'shunt active power filter' hits — electrical engineering, NOT CSF shunts. Real patents/papers, but off-topic.

schema.rejection_axis: which of the 6 equivalence axes failed

purpose: Prevents silent discarding of irrelevant results (auditability)
Documents that the search WAS executed (proves coverage)
Provides evidence for patent counsel that false positives were considered
Enables learning — patterns of false positives can improve future queries

state_separation_v2.principle: A mechanism can be technically poor while patent coverage remains incomplete. Engineering and patent states are ALWAYS independent.
state_separation_v2.v8_example: Territory #4 V8: ENGINEERING = CEILING (derivative does not beat instantaneous ΔP) but PATENT = SEARCH_INCOMPLETE (Compendex unavailable, PatSnap family/citations failed).
state_separation_v2.critical_rule: Engineering CEILING → BELOW_BUYER_THRESHOLD regardless of patent state. A novel mechanism that doesn't work is still not buyer-grade.

alternative_defeated_ledger.purpose: Every rejected alternative becomes part of the invention's provenance. Demonstrates that the invention was attacked, not just supported.

examples_from_current_work.same_problem_test: SAME_PROBLEM_SAME_MECHANISM (both classify shunt state from active features)
examples_from_current_work.comparator: B - A = -0.5pp (ML does NOT improve active)
examples_from_current_work.result: alternative_defeated (ML does not improve; threshold sufficient)
examples_from_current_work.why_rejected: ML adds complexity without benefit. Family D rejected.

examples_from_current_work.alternative_description: Intrathecal polymeric nanocomposite hydrogel for drug delivery

same_problem_test.axis_1_objective: mismatch (SCI drug delivery vs CSF drainage + retention)
same_problem_test.axis_3_constraints: mismatch (no drainage constraint vs drainage maintained)

examples_from_current_work.comparator: N/A — neighboring problem, no engineering comparator needed
examples_from_current_work.result: alternative_neighboring (does not solve same coupled problem)
examples_from_current_work.why_rejected: Hydrogel is a sustained-release depot, not a size-selective filtration element. Does not preserve drainage. Position #2b rejected.

examples_from_current_work.alternative_description: Predictive trajectory controller (state estimation + prediction + proactive control)
examples_from_current_work.same_problem_test: SAME_PROBLEM_DIFFERENT_MECHANISM (both regulate CSF drainage, but predictive vs instantaneous)
examples_from_current_work.evidence: V7_PREDICTIVE_SIMULATION.json — C4 vs C3: M4 reduction = 0%, M1 reduction = 1%
examples_from_current_work.comparator: C4 dominates C3 in only 1/9 states
examples_from_current_work.why_rejected: Predictive controller CEILING — does not materially outperform instantaneous ΔP. V7 frozen.

fda_clinical_reservation.ceo_directive: Do not add FDA/clinical/post-market into the live 1-10 discovery loop yet. Reserve as final portfolio reality audit.
exclusion_from_discovery_loop: MAUDE is passive surveillance with causality/quality limitations — NOT a simplistic score input
ClinicalTrials.gov is structured human-evidence audit data — NOT merely 'clinical validation'
Both should be an ADVERSARIAL REALITY LAYER, not a discovery input

data_sources: FDA MAUDE — adverse event reports for predicate devices (e.g., Medtronic Strata, Sophysa Polaris)
ClinicalTrials.gov — study results and adverse events for competing approaches
FDA De Novo database — novel device classifications
audit_questions: Do predicate devices have adverse events that our mechanism could prevent?
Do competing clinical trials reveal safety signals we missed?
Is our regulatory pathway (510(k) vs De Novo) supported by predicate landscape?
Are there post-market surveillance findings that change our risk assessment?
final_audit_scope.audit_output: FINAL_PORTFOLIO_REALITY_AUDIT.json — adversarial reality layer applied to all 10 territories

fda_clinical_reservation.rationale: Discovery loop (1-10) focuses on mechanism + patent. Clinical reality is applied AFTER, as adversarial audit, to prevent survivorship bias.
